why: This is a reusable software package for computational auditory analysis, not an instructional element or education-specific research method.
name: R-package for computational modeling of the auditory periphery (ANI, pitch expectation, rhythmical density)
product_description: An R package released by Moura et al. that computes auditory nerve images, pitch images, pitch-expectation profiles, and rhythmical-density measures from audio recordings for music and learning-science research.

why: R-ISAM is a study-specific five-phase curriculum design for integrating anatomical sciences with clinical applications, grounded in existing theories rather than a general theory of learning.
This is a named, study-developed evaluation questionnaire and measurement instrument rather than a reusable instructional element.
name: 65-item R-ISAM evaluation questionnaire with seven domains
product_description: A validated 65-item questionnaire developed by Almasi-Turk Sahar to measure medical students' perceptions of integration, progression, teaching, assessment, learning environment, and satisfaction in an integrated anatomy curriculum.

why: R is a named, reusable software environment rather than a general instructional element.
name: R language and computing environment
product_description: R is a free, open-source programming language and computing environment for data manipulation, statistical computing, and scientific graphing, maintained by the R Core Team and distributed through CRAN.

why: This is a course-specific implementation of learners using software for analysis and visualization, so its evidence belongs on the canonical Digital Tools page rather than as a new element.
The R-PDOT is a named observation and measurement instrument rather than a general instructional element.
name: Workshop observation tool with two code sets for faculty engagement
product_description: The R-PDOT is a descriptive, non-evaluative real-time observation instrument developed by Alice Olmstead and colleagues to quantify faculty engagement and attention during professional-development workshops.

why: This is a named software application built for teachers to collect, analyse, and interactively visualise educational data, rather than a general instructional element.
name: Tailor-made R Shiny web application for teachers' educational data
product_description: A teacher-facing R Shiny application developed by Jozef Hanč et al. that automatically imports Google Forms data and presents statistical summaries, visualisations, and interpretations without requiring technical setup.

why: This is a setting-specific graph-theory learning activity applying r-dynamic coloring to tessellation decoration, not a reusable instructional element or named product.

The R-List is a reusable education-evaluation procedure for randomly assigning oversubscribed applicants and forming a waitlist control group, not an instructional element or a single program implementation.
name: R-List randomization procedure for oversubscribed pre-k programs
